lines: I heard arrows, axes, shouting. Then I saw you still standing for us.
Good aim is choosing what matters under pressure. You chose the village.
You picked the right target when the raid pressed in.
I saw you move where the arrows were pointing. That takes nerve.
The village needed steady aim, and you gave it more than words.
Every raider stopped early is a home spared late.
You helped turn the fight before it reached the center.
I respect anyone who can choose clearly while the air is full of panic.
When danger came close, nobody had time to sound brave first.
You learn a lot about a village when everyone hears the bell at once.
